newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian sugar prices rise on lower quota fears.
newsitem.headline: Indian sugar prices rise on lower quota fears.

text.p: Indian sugar prices gained on Thursday on fears that the government may announce a lower free sale quota for January, dealers said.
Consumer demand was low. Ready delivery sugar S-30 rose by 20 rupees to 1,215/1,265 rupees while M-30 climbed up by 10/20 rupees to 1,260/1,340 rupees.

"The free sale quota for the current month is 800,000 tonnes while traders are expecting a quota of about 675,000/725,000 tonnes next month," one broker said. "Limited arrivals from mills also helped the market to bounce back," he said.
